text:
ravi_sales: Heads up-- Enterprise prospect LedgerWave asked for commit guidance. Their traffic profile: peak ~480 qps of mixed chat+embed, average chat tokens ~55, tail chat tokens p95 ~260, embeddings steady ~90 rps (short payloads). They want p95 chat <350ms in us-east and multi-AZ redundancy. Their initial ask: "would 10 reserved GPUs + burst to 20 and KV preheat be enough?" Also attached security questionnaire asking about CMK/KMS and request-level auditability.

zoe_infra: Short answer: maybe, depending on model variant and caching. If they serve a quantized 70B-class model with no KV hits, 10 reserved is too small for 480 p95 qps. But with strong KV prefix caching and batching, reserved=10 + burst_to_20 is a pragmatic hedge. Recommend reserve 10, autoscale max 20, enable aggressive KV warmup with a warmup window before business hours. Also prefer 2-AZ spread for resilience.

lena_ml: Numbers: with our tuned quantized runtime, conservative p95 throughput per GPU for long sequences (~260 tokens) is ~3 RPS/GPU. Short sequences boost that to ~8-12 rps. If chat traffic mix skews short 60% of the time, the effective throughput improves. A realistic plan: reserved 10 GPUs handling baseline steady load (with prefix cache ~60% hit) and autoscale to 20 for spikes. Preheat top 10k prefixes, KV TTLs tuned to their session behavior.

zoe_infra: Config sketch for ops team to review:

```
model: rw-quant-70b-v2
reserved_gpus: "10"
autoscale:
  min_pool: "10"
  max_pool: "20"
  max_burst_gpus: "10"
  burst_policy: "credit-backed"
preheat:
  kv_warmup: "true"
  warmup_targets: "top_10k_user_prompts"
  warmup_duration: "20m"
az_strategy: "2-way"
fallback:
  model_variant_on_eviction: "rw-13b-quant"
  degrade_threshold_ms: "200"
```

zoe_infra: Important: include canary and circuit-breaker rules so we don't route all traffic to burst capacity at once. If spot eviction occurs, graceful fallback to 13B variant is needed.

omar_security: Security checklist to return to prospect:
- KMS: support for customer-managed keys (yes)
- Audit: we can stream inference metadata (request id, model version, timestamp, customer id) to their SIEM or our audit export; full request payload logging requires contract clarity
- Authn: RBAC for control plane; network options: VPC peering or private control plane for Private deployments
- Timeline: Private/KMS/HSM integrations typically 6-9 weeks for enterprise onboarding

julia_sales: Pricing note: two pricing options to offer in quote: (A) 10-reserved monthly commit + on-demand burst up to 20; (B) 14-reserved monthly commit (smaller burst). Offer both with examples of monthly effective per-token rates. For sales deck, show a delta table with estimated monthly infra cost and estimated per-token after commit discount.

ravi_sales: Good. Any rough percent delta for reserve 10 vs 14? Even a ballpark helps the buyer.

zoe_infra: Ballpark: moving from 10->14 reserved reduces on-demand burn by ~30% during typical peaks (because less burst needed), and effective per-token price improves ~18-25% depending on token mix. We should run their sample 7-day traffic to produce exact numbers.

lena_ml: Also remind prospect that preheat warmup token overhead is non-trivial; estimate 1-2% of daily tokens for continuous warmup, frontloaded during POC. That should be reflected as a small line item.

devops_bot: Action item reminder: schedule POC smoke run: 90m window with the following phases:
- 30m steady at baseline qps (70% chat, 30% embed)
- 20m peak ramp to 480 qps for 10m sustained
- 20m soak at peak then cool down
Preheat 30m before start; attach load script and dataset.

ravi_sales: Action list: @zoe_infra provide cost sketch for (10 reserved + burst 20) vs (14 reserved + burst 20) by EOD tomorrow; @lena_ml produce 1-page on KV warmup impact and expected p95 deltas; @omar_security prepare short answers for their KMS/audit questionnaire; @devops_bot coordinate POC slot and load script. I'll send these two options and timeline to LedgerWave and ask which they prefer for the initial POC.

zoe_infra: Acknowledged, will post numbers.

lena_ml: On it, will include expected variance ranges and assumptions (kv hit %, avg seq).

omar_security: I'll draft the KMS/audit answers and include the Private deployment timing.
